review: S14 MCP durable save contract and security
verified: The strict save_document input and exact eight-tool public surface remain unchanged in source stdio, HTTP, and generated bundle; the existing MCP contract regression passed.

Both transports call the shared saveDocumentToStore adapter and retain canonical JSON in MCP content[0].text. The published response reports queued and an optional jobId only after an accepted owner transaction; published files with failed or lost ACK retain enqueue_failed, retryable warning, and no jobId.
New save calls require a vacant destination; two same-content saves under a fixed clock allocate distinct contained paths, while explicit same-intent replay reuses the original publication.

The configured lexical source identity and canonical publication root remain equivalent across junction roots. A real owner transaction preserves a seeded lexical source, and retry preserves document identity, desired revision, and job identity.

Private intent provenance omits metadata recoverable from saved frontmatter. gitContextPath validation, transient use, and redaction behavior are unchanged; no raw path or credential was added to the public envelope.
The S14 main-process save path publishes the file and delegates SQLite acceptance to OwnerWorkerController, without calling the legacy queueDocumentIndex path.
scopeLimit: This review covers the S14 adapter and frozen source hash. Legacy producer migration, packaged Electron smoke, and simultaneous legacy-writer stress are later work identified in the S14 evidence; this review does not mark REL-DOC-009 as fully verified.
